title: Fix hardcoded DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS — chart uses 20/100/300 for every asset
problem: The chart's threshold price-lines and the 'now' latest-value coloring are driven by DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS = {drift 20, depeg 100, critical 300} hardcoded at page.tsx:56 and passed at :216. But the rail, alert policy, and dashboard all use per-asset thresholdsFor(symbol, class) (asset-rail.tsx:111, synced to assets.toml). So for sUSD (drift 275/depeg 500/critical 800 bps) the chart draws the drift line at -20bps and paints a +1.37%-PEGGED asset as 'depeg' red while the rail correctly reads PEGGED. Same class-band trust bug fixed for the dashboard peek (Fix 4), still live on the chart.
recommendation: Replace DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS with thresholdsFor(asset.symbol, asset.class) from lib/alerts/policy.ts and pass the per-asset object into AssetChart (page.tsx:216). The chart already accepts a {drift_bps,depeg_bps,critical_bps} prop (asset-chart.tsx:52) so it's one call-site swap plus deleting the constant. Removes a direct contradiction between the chart and the rail on the same screen.
reference: Internal consistency with Fix 4 (class-specific drift band) shipped on the dashboard peek; assets.toml source of truth
implementation_note: Import thresholdsFor from @/lib/alerts/policy, replace thresholds={DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS} at :216 with thresholds={thresholdsFor(asset.symbol, asset.class)}, delete DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS at :56. No AssetChart change needed. Verify on sUSD (+1.37% must show neutral/text, not red) and INF (~-1.18%, drift line at -140 not -20). addThresholdLines only draws negative-side lines, so for positive-spread sUSD the lines won't appear — acceptable; the latestColor coloring is the part that was actively wrong. The single highest-ROI item in the batch.

title: Peg-jitter / dispersion signal in the hero + rail (series_24h, zero new data)
problem: The hero and rail show current spread, drift floor, 24h range, median and worst spread — but NOT dispersion/jitter, the difference between an asset sitting steadily at -1.2% (healthy structural discount) and one whipsawing 0% to -2.4% (unstable). A steady-but-off asset and a jittery asset can show identical current spread and identical worst spread yet very different risk. The data is free: every payload ships series_24h inline (types.ts:34, ~25 fractional spreads).
recommendation: Add a 'stability/jitter' helper to lib/api/format.ts computing stdev (or MAD) of series_24h, bucket it (tight/loose/erratic), and surface it as (a) a 5th KPI in the AssetRail Health block (asset-rail.tsx:162-183, currently 4 KPIs) and (b) a sub-line under the hero spread next to drift floor (asset-hero-v2.tsx:156-163). The Pyth confidence-band intuition reduced to one number, zero backend change.
reference: Pyth confidence band (widening = more uncertainty) reduced to a scalar; series_24h inline, dispersion purely client-side
implementation_note: Add pegJitterBps(series: number[]): number to lib/api/format.ts computing stdev (or MAD) of series.map(x=>x*10000), bucket tight/loose/erratic. Surface as a 5th RailKpi (:162-183) and a sub-line under the hero spread (asset-hero-v2.tsx:156-163, next to drift floor). Guard for series_24h undefined/short (<3 pts) -> render '—'; multiply fractional spreads by 10000 for bps before stdev. Shared helper with peg-jitter-stability-column — unblocks the screener jitter column.

title: Recovery-confidence rubric breakdown + HelpIcon + 'calibrating' badge
problem: RecoveryConfidence shows a single A-D grade + a 100-pt gauge + prose, but the SCORING is opaque: the additive rubric (peg-time max 50, flips max 25, peer-convergence max 25) lives only in code comments (recovery-confidence.tsx:105-116). Worse, during calibration the alert stream is empty, so flips=0 and recoveryP50 is null — the gauge silently awards 'flips 25/25' and a flattering grade off MISSING data (recovery-confidence.tsx:111), the 'absence != confirmation' trap. No HelpIcon, no signal the grade is provisional.
recommendation: (1) Render the three sub-scores as labeled bars/chips (peg-time X/50, stability X/25, peer-convergence X/25) so the grade is auditable. (2) Add a HelpIcon on the H2 (:190) — needs a new 'recovery_confidence' GLOSSARY entry. (3) When alerts is empty AND recoveryP50 is null, show a 'calibrating' badge and grey/down-weight the stability sub-score instead of crediting a full 25 for the absence of data. Mirrors the Status-page calibration honesty.
reference: DeFi-Monitor persistence rubric + Chaos Labs severity-indicator breakdown; internal Status calibration honesty
implementation_note: Core fix in compute() (:105-116): when alerts is empty/undefined treat flips-credit as UNKNOWN (e.g. a neutral 15, like the peerSpread==null path) rather than a full 25, and surface a 'calibrating' chip when alerts?.length===0 && recoveryP50Min==null. Add a new GLOSSARY entry + extend the GlossaryTerm union before adding <HelpIcon term='recovery_confidence'> on the H2. A Facts row already exists (:202-207), so the sub-score bars are secondary polish — scope to the calibrating-badge + down-weight-missing-data as the core. This panel windows on 7d alerts, not 24h.

title: Add error + empty states (the page currently has NEITHER)
problem: useAssets() returns { data, isLoading, error, mutate } but /assets destructures only { data, isLoading } (assets/page.tsx:51) — so when the backend is unreachable the page shows the loading skeleton FOREVER, and when a filter/search matches nothing the row map (line 133) silently renders an empty list with no message. The dashboard already solved both (BackendDownState at dashboard/page.tsx:464; 'No assets match this filter' empty copy). /assets is the most-likely-deep-linked-cold surface, so a dead skeleton is the worst place to lack an error state.
recommendation: Destructure { data, isLoading, error, mutate }. Render BackendDownState (extract from dashboard/page.tsx:464 into a shared component) when error && !assets, with onRetry={()=>mutate()}. Render an explicit empty state ('No assets match "{q}" / this filter — clear search') when !isLoading && filtered.length===0.
reference: Dashboard BackendDownState + 'No assets match this filter' empty copy (dashboard/page.tsx:464, :246)
implementation_note: Destructure {data, isLoading, error, mutate} at assets/page.tsx:51. Extract BackendDownState from dashboard/page.tsx:464-491 into web/components/molecules/ (self-contained, deps are Link+cn) and import in both. Render it when error && !assets with onRetry={()=>mutate()}; render an explicit empty state when !isLoading && filtered.length===0. title: Decision: keep /assets and make it a genuine analyst screener (do NOT redirect to /dashboard)
problem: The deferred backlog frames this as an OR: 'make /assets a real screener OR redirect to dashboard'. Today /assets is a flatter, weaker clone of the dashboard table, so the redirect temptation is real. But the dashboard is a 3-pane peek-driven WORKBENCH locked to lg+ (hidden lg:grid at dashboard/page.tsx:186; mobile gets a stripped MobileAssetRow with no sparkline/sort/peek). A redirect would (a) throw tablet/mobile users into the phone fallback, (b) collapse a deep-linkable URL-sortable table into a hover workbench, and (c) lose the canonical /assets URL analysts bookmark.
recommendation: Commit to /assets as the canonical full-universe SCREENER and differentiate it by ROLE: dashboard = live peek workbench (lg+, hover, 3-pane); /assets = scannable, sortable, URL-stateful, mobile-first table at every breakpoint. Resolves the OR by argument: the two surfaces answer different questions ('what is moving right now, let me peek' vs 'rank/scan/sort the whole universe and deep-link a view').
reference: DefiLlama keeps /stablecoins screener AND /stablecoin/[id] detail pages as distinct surfaces, not a redirect
implementation_note: This is a decision record, not a code change. Capture in the audit REPORT and proceed with the dependent proposals (sortable headers, search, sparkline/jitter/safety columns). No file to touch. It ships zero pixels alone but gates every other /assets proposal.

title: Peg-stability / jitter column computed from series_24h dispersion
problem: Two assets can show the SAME instantaneous spread but behave totally differently: one steady-off-peg, one whipsawing. The screener shows only the point-in-time spread, so it can't surface a jittery-but-currently-calm asset — the leading indicator of stress. The data is fully inline (series_24h, ~25 fractional spreads), zero backend change.
recommendation: Add a pegJitter(series) helper next to cleanSeries (format.ts:104) returning a dispersion stat — standard deviation OR max-abs-range over the 24h window, in bps. Render a 'Jitter' column ('±18 bps' or a 3-dot calm/choppy/volatile glyph) and make it sortable. Pair the instantaneous spread with this windowed stability — DefiLlama's '% Off Peg' + '1m % Off Peg' two-column pattern. Color-ramp so a volatile asset reads hot even when momentarily pegged.
reference: DefiLlama '% Off Peg' + '1m % Off Peg' paired columns; DeFi-Monitor persistence-of-deviation leading indicator
implementation_note: Add pegJitter(series:number[]):number to format.ts beside cleanSeries (:104) returning pstdev (or max-min range) of cleanSeries(series) in bps. Decide ONE stat (recommend stdev — range is dominated by single outliers like INF's 126bps tick) and document it so it doesn't drift from the sort semantics. Verified differentiated across the live universe (sd 0.8-2.7bps, distinct from worst-|s|). Highest differentiation-per-line on the list; shared helper with peg-jitter-signal-detail.

title: aria-live region announcing peg-state transitions (screen-reader-silent today)

When an asset flips PEGGED->DRIFT live a screen-reader user gets nothing. aria-live exists ONLY in events/page, mock-data-banner, health-banner — nowhere in the dashboard tree.

The single highest-integrity a11y gap on a live risk monitor.

title: Wire EngineFlowStrip to lastHeartbeatAt (true liveness, not socket-open)
problem: EngineFlowStrip reads ONLY `connected` from useLive (engine-flow-strip.tsx:24,30) and shows a green 'Ingesting N assets' pulse purely off socket-open. It never reads lastHeartbeatAt (live-context.tsx:69,136). Between heartbeats the strip can read confidently green while the feed is idling. The 'Tick 1.2s' label and the 1.2s bar animation are decorative hardcodes with no relation to the real ~5s engine heartbeat — the headline live indicator is theater, on a trust product.
recommendation: Pass lastHeartbeatAt into EngineFlowStrip and derive liveness from heartbeat age: green <~8s, amber 'feed quiet' 8-15s, grey 'reconnecting' beyond (matching status/page.tsx:101-103). Pulse FROM actual heartbeat arrival (key off lastHeartbeatAt) instead of a free-running CSS loop. Replace the fictional 'Tick 1.2s' with the real cadence or a live age readout. Honor reduced-motion.
reference: Pyth/uptime status-dot conventions (color maps to measured freshness); the project's own status page implements heartbeat-age thresholds
implementation_note: Pass lastHeartbeatAt from dashboard/page.tsx (add it to the useLive destructure at line 55) into EngineFlowStrip. Compute age = Date.now() - Date.parse(lastHeartbeatAt) on a ~1s interval (setInterval+state). Map green<8s / amber 8-15s / grey>15s to match status/page.tsx:101-103. Replace 'Tick 1.2s' with 'beat Ns ago'. lastHeartbeatAt is server-clock ISO — guard against clock skew (don't show negative ages). Key the CSS pulse off lastHeartbeatAt so it pulses on real beats. (Overlaps live-heartbeat-pulse-updated-ago — same wiring; ship as one.)

title: Tick-flash GSAP tween must honor prefers-reduced-motion
problem: The global reduced-motion guard (globals.css:205) only neutralizes CSS animations/transitions. Pairs with the token proposal so reduced users still see the value update, just without the strobe.
reference: WCAG 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions; house useReducedMotionGsap centralizes this detection
implementation_note: At the top of the effect (after line 24) check window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches; if reduced, skip the tween or do an instant gsap.set(node,{color}) then a setTimeout restore with no interpolation. Don't import useReducedMotionGsap here (calling matchMedia directly is simpler in this already-effect context). Build AFTER tick-flash-token so the single token also gives one dimming knob. A genuine WCAG defect, not polish.

title: App-shell entrance choreography (MotionConfig + restrained pane cascade)
problem: The 3-pane dashboard hard-cuts in: sidebar, table header, EngineFlowStrip, rows and peek all paint in the same frame with zero choreography.
